evals.prompt: Print an A1 family tree poster of Caroline Kennedy's ancestors - she was born 27 Nov 1957. Put in every generation you have.
evals.expected_output: Identifies person 36 without asking, collects with --locale en, reports the summary in English (64 ancestors, 8 generations, about 9 pt on A1 at full depth), shows the verification table, proposes removing the nickname from John Francis "Honey Fitz" Fitzgerald, waits for confirmation; after the simulated answer 'looks good' renders SVG+PDF at full depth.
expectations: Conversation is in English and collect runs with --locale en
Person 36 is identified without a disambiguation question
Table dates use the English form, e.g. '29 May 1917'
Suffixes are kept: 'John Vernou Bouvier III', 'John Vernou Bouvier Jr.'
Surnames print in normal case ('John Fitzgerald Kennedy', not 'KENNEDY') and the '(-----)' placeholders print as an empty surname
Proposes removing the nickname "Honey Fitz" from the given names
Mentions that James Fitzgerald appears twice in the tree
Chart title is 'Ancestors of Caroline Bouvier Kennedy'
Does not render before the user confirms the data
Renders all 8 generations and boxes print 'b.' and 'd.' lines

evals.prompt: Ich möchte eine Ahnentafel von John Fitzgerald Kennedy zum Ausdrucken. Bitte 3 Generationen.
evals.expected_output: Two matches (person 4, born 1917, and person 37, Jr., born 1960) -> asks in German which one is meant, listing birth dates and parents; after the simulated answer 'den Präsidenten, geboren 1917' uses person 4 with --locale de, depth 3.
expectations: Asks a disambiguation question in German listing both John Fitzgerald Kennedy candidates
Collects person 4 with --locale de
Table and render use --depth 3; Patrick Kennedy (born about 1823) is among the deepest ancestors
Dates use the German form, e.g. '29.5.1917' and 'um 1823', and boxes use '*' and '†'
Chart title is in German, e.g. 'Vorfahren von John Fitzgerald Kennedy'

evals.prompt: Vytiskni mi rodokmen Josepha Patricka Kennedyho, narozeného 1888.
evals.expected_output: Three people named Joseph Patrick Kennedy, but only person 1 was born in 1888; only a year was given -> asks in Czech for a quick confirmation; after 'ano' collects with --locale cs, Czech table and chart, title declined into the genitive.
expectations: Conversation is in Czech
Asks for confirmation of person 1 before collecting, because only the birth year was given
Collects with --locale cs; dates like '6.9.1888' and 'kol. 1823', boxes use 'n.' and 'z.'
Chart title is declined, e.g. 'Rodina Josepha Patricka Kennedyho'

evals.prompt: Je voudrais imprimer l'arbre généalogique de Rose Elizabeth Fitzgerald, née le 22 juillet 1890.
evals.expected_output: No bundled French locale -> copies locales/en.json into the person's directory, translates every key into French, identifies person 2 without asking, collects with --locale pointing at that file; no missing-keys warning.
expectations: Conversation is in French
Creates a French locale file under family-trees/<slug>/ and passes its path to --locale
collect prints no 'missing keys filled from English' warning
Dates use French month names, e.g. '22 juillet 1890'
The table headers, review notes and chart title are in French

evals.expected_output: The request reveals no language -> asks which language to use for the conversation and the chart before collecting anything.
expectations: Asks for the language before running collect
Mentions that any language is possible
